description: CMMC Level 2 Infra Command Registry — Azure GCC High Tenant Onboarding

entries.label: Register Required Azure Resource Providers
entries.notes: Registers 11 Azure resource providers required for the CMMC L2 infrastructure stack (Sentinel, Key Vault, Storage, Network, Compute, etc.). Idempotent — re-registration of already-registered providers is a no-op. Evidence proves the subscription is ready for resource provisioning.

entries.label: Set Azure Subscription Context
entries.get_command: Get-AzContext | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subscription | Where-Object { $_.Id -eq '{subscriptionId}' } | Select-Object Id,Name | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Sets the Az PowerShell session to the target Azure Gov subscription. Evidence confirms the operator is working in the correct subscription boundary, satisfying SC.L1-3.13.1 boundary monitoring requirements.

entries.label: Create Azure Resource Group
entries.notes: Creates the primary resource group with CMMC L2 tags (environment=cmmc-l2, managed_by=bhd-stamper). All subsequent infrastructure resources are deployed into this resource group. Evidence proves a dedicated, tagged container exists for CUI-scoped resources.

entries.label: Assign CMMC L2 Azure Policy Initiative
entries.set_command: $policySetDef = Get-AzPolicySetDefinition -Id '/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/policySetDefinitions/4e50fd13-098b-3206-61d6-d1d78205cb45'; $existing = Get-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'CMMC-L2-Initiative' -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (-not $existing) { New-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'CMMC-L2-Initiative' -DisplayName 'CMMC Level 2 Requirements' -PolicySetDefinition $policySetDef -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}' -IdentityType 'SystemAssigned' -Location '{location}' } else { Write-Output 'Assignment already exists - skipping creation' }
entries.get_command: Get-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'CMMC-L2-Initiative' -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, DisplayName, EnforcementMode | ConvertTo-Json
evidence_commands: Get-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'CMMC-L2-Initiative' -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, DisplayName, EnforcementMode | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Assigns the built-in CMMC Level 2 policy initiative (policy set 4e50fd13-098b-3206-61d6-d1d78205cb45) at the tenant's subscription, with a system-assigned identity in the tenant's region. Subscription and region come from the tenant variables (QUESTIONS P-11).

entries.label: Defender for Cloud at the free tier (Foundational CSPM)
entries.set_command: foreach ($p in @('VirtualMachines','StorageAccounts','CloudPosture','Arm')) { $cur = Get-AzSecurityPricing -Name $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (-not $cur -or $cur.PricingTier -ne 'Standard') { Set-AzSecurityPricing -Name $p -PricingTier 'Free' | Out-Null } }; Get-AzSecurityPricing | Where-Object { $_.Name -in @('VirtualMachines','StorageAccounts','CloudPosture','Arm') } | Select-Object Name,PricingTier | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Free by default (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §3.7; Muster manifest resource sec-defender, tier Free). Sets the four plans to the free tier, which keeps Foundational CSPM (posture recommendations) on at no cost, and never downgrades a plan the customer already pays for (Standard is left as found). The paid plans (threat detection, SI.L2-3.14.6[a]) are the opt-in recurring entry AZ-FOUND-005.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: 10 GB/month ingestion; 90-day retention (inside the free window)

entries.label: Create Log Analytics Workspace (90-day retention)
entries.notes: Creates the central Log Analytics workspace with 90-day retention, inside the free interactive window (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §3.7; Muster manifest LAW_RETENTION_DAYS = 90). Long-term evidence retention is the WORM storage days (AZ-LOG-002/003), not the workspace. Ingestion is still billed, so the entry is recurring and off by default. Captures lawWorkspaceId and lawResourceId for downstream Sentinel and diagnostic entries. PerGB2018 is the only SKU in Azure Government.

entries.label: Create Immutable Log Storage Account
entries.notes: Creates an immutable log storage account with TLS 1.2 minimum, HTTPS-only traffic, and no public blob access. Serves as the secondary audit log store for WORM-locked evidence containers. Captures storageResourceId for downstream RBAC and diagnostic settings.

entries.label: Assign System Managed Identity to Storage Account
entries.notes: Assigns a system-managed identity to the log storage account so it can authenticate to Key Vault for CMK encryption without storing credentials. Captures storageMiPrincipalId for the RBAC role assignment in AZ-LOG-002b. Evidence proves identity-based access is configured per SC.L2-3.13.10.

entries.label: Grant Storage MI Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User Role
entries.set_command: New-AzRoleAssignment -RoleDefinitionName 'Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User' -ObjectId '{storageMiPrincipalId}' -Scope '{kvResourceId}'
entries.get_command: Get-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{storageMiPrincipalId}' -Scope '{kvResourceId}' | Where-Object RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User' | Select-Object RoleDefinitionName,ObjectId,Scope,RoleAssignmentId -First 1 | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3

evidence.equals: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User

checks.equals: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User

entries.notes: Grants the storage account managed identity the Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User role, enabling customer-managed key (CMK) envelope encryption. This RBAC assignment must propagate before AZ-LOG-002c can apply CMK encryption. Evidence proves least-privilege cryptographic key access. PH-12 (P12-R5): the GET and the evidence read the role assignment as JSON, and the rule checks the role and its scope; the evidence used Get-AzKeyVaultAccessPolicy, which is not an Az cmdlet (the simulator could not answer it, and Azure would not either), and the rule read $.ResourceId, which a role assignment does not carry.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: customer-managed key: Key Vault operations billed per use

entries.label: Enable CMK Encryption on Storage Account
entries.notes: Enables customer-managed key (CMK) encryption on the log storage account using an RSA-HSM key in Key Vault. Satisfies SC.L2-3.13.10 cryptographic key management and SC.L2-3.13.16 CUI-at-rest protection. Evidence proves KeySource is Microsoft.Keyvault rather than Microsoft-managed.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: storage only, cannot be undone while locked

entries.label: Set Storage Container Immutability Policy (WORM)
entries.notes: WORM lock is irreversible. Operator must review get_command output before live execution. If PolicyState is Locked, this step must be skipped manually — do not re-run.

entries.label: Create Key Vault (purge-protection enabled)
entries.notes: Creates a Standard Azure Key Vault (founder ruling OQ-4: Standard by default, HSM opt-in) with purge protection, RBAC authorization and deployment disabled. Captures kvResourceId and kvUri for downstream CMK and RBAC entries. Key Vault is billed per use, which counts as recurring (CQ-2): off by default, behind DP-1 and DP-2. SC.L2-3.13.10 has free evidence without it (SC.L2-3.13.10.key-escrow).

entries.label: Assign Key Vault Crypto Officer Role to EO Service Principal
entries.set_command: $assignment = New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{eoSpObjectId}' -RoleDefinitionName 'Key Vault Crypto Officer' -Scope (Get-AzKeyVault -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -VaultName '{keyVaultName}').ResourceId; Write-Host 'RBAC assignment created, waiting 5 minutes for propagation...'; Start-Sleep -Seconds 300; $assignment
entries.notes: Assigns the EO service principal the Key Vault Crypto Officer role for automated key lifecycle management. Includes a 300-second propagation delay for Azure RBAC to replicate. Evidence proves the automation identity has least-privilege cryptographic access per AC.L1-3.1.1.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: 1 software RSA 4096 key, billed per use (CQ-2)

entries.label: Create CMK Key in Key Vault (software RSA 4096)
entries.set_command: Add-AzKeyVaultKey -VaultName '{keyVaultName}' -Name '{cmkKeyName}' -Destination Software -KeyType RSA -Size 4096 -KeyOps @('wrapKey','unwrapKey') -WarningAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name,Version,Enabled,Id,@{N='KeyType';E={$_.Key.Kty}},@{N='KeySize';E={$_.KeySize}},@{N='KeyOps';E={$_.Key.KeyOps}} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
entries.notes: Software-protected RSA 4096 key in a Standard vault (founder ruling OQ-4: Standard Key Vault by default, HSM opt-in; Muster manifest resource sto-cmk). Key Vault is billed per use, which counts as recurring (CQ-2), so this stays behind DP-1 and DP-2. An HSM key needs a Premium vault and is not offered by default (open item: an HSM opt-in entry). Capture cmkKeyVersion is reserved for key rotation tracking.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: opt-in: Premium vault + 1 HSM-protected RSA key version, billed per key version and per use

entries.label: Opt-in: HSM-protected CMK Key (Premium vault)
entries.set_command: $r = Invoke-AzRestMethod -Method PATCH -Path '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroup}/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/{keyVaultName}?api-version=2023-07-01' -Payload '{"properties":{"sku":{"family":"A","name":"premium"}}}'; if ($r.StatusCode -ge 300) { throw ('Key Vault SKU change failed: ' + $r.StatusCode) }; Add-AzKeyVaultKey -VaultName '{keyVaultName}' -Name '{cmkKeyName}-hsm' -Destination HSM -KeyType RSA -Size 3072 -KeyOps @('wrapKey','unwrapKey') -WarningAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name,Version,Enabled,Id,@{N='KeyType';E={$_.Key.Kty}} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
entries.notes: Opt-in only (founder ruling OQ-4: Standard Key Vault by default, HSM opt-in; SP-12). Moves the vault to the Premium SKU (no standing charge) and adds an HSM-protected RSA 3072 key beside the software key of AZ-KV-003. HSM key versions are billed monthly, so this is recurring: off by default, behind DP-1 and DP-2, and planned only together with AZ-KV-001 (cost_gate.requires_entries). The default is the software key, AZ-KV-003. Not served by the simulator.

entries.label: Create Virtual Network
entries.notes: Creates the primary VNet in Azure Gov with the specified CIDR range. This VNet provides the network boundary for all CUI-scoped workloads, satisfying SC.L1-3.13.1 boundary protection and SC.L1-3.13.5 subnet segmentation requirements.

entries.label: Create Management Subnet
entries.set_command: $vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}'; $existing = $vnet.Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'snet-mgmt'}; if (-not $existing) { Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name 'snet-mgmt' -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix '{mgmtSubnetCidr}' | Set-AzVirtualNetwork } else { Write-Output 'snet-mgmt subnet already exists' }
entries.get_command: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'snet-mgmt'} | Select-Object -First 1 Name, AddressPrefix | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
evidence_commands: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Select-Object Name, AddressPrefix
entries.notes: Creates the management subnet (snet-mgmt) within the VNet for administrative access paths. Segmentation from workload and bastion subnets satisfies SC.L1-3.13.5 network segmentation. Evidence proves the subnet exists with the correct CIDR range.

entries.label: Create Workload Subnet
entries.set_command: $vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}'; $existing = $vnet.Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'snet-workload'}; if (-not $existing) { Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name 'snet-workload' -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix '{workloadSubnetCidr}' | Set-AzVirtualNetwork } else { Write-Output 'snet-workload subnet already exists' }
entries.get_command: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'snet-workload'} | Select-Object -First 1 Name, AddressPrefix | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
evidence_commands: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Select-Object Name, AddressPrefix
entries.notes: Creates the workload subnet (snet-workload) for CUI-processing resources. This subnet receives the NSG association (AZ-NSG-005) enforcing deny-all-by-default traffic rules per SC.L2-3.13.6. Evidence proves the subnet exists with the correct CIDR range.

entries.label: Create AzureBastionHost Subnet
entries.set_command: $vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}'; $existing = $vnet.Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'AzureBastionSubnet'}; if (-not $existing) { Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name 'AzureBastionSubnet' -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix '{bastionSubnetCidr}' | Set-AzVirtualNetwork } else { Write-Output 'AzureBastionSubnet already exists' }
entries.get_command: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'AzureBastionSubnet'} | Select-Object -First 1 Name, AddressPrefix | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
evidence_commands: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Select-Object Name, AddressPrefix
entries.notes: Creates the AzureBastionSubnet, which is a required named subnet for Azure Bastion deployment. Bastion provides secure RDP/SSH access without exposing VMs to public IPs, satisfying SC.L1-3.13.1 boundary protection. The subnet name "AzureBastionSubnet" is mandated by Azure.

entries.label: Create AzureFirewall Subnet
entries.set_command: $vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}'; $existing = $vnet.Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'AzureFirewallSubnet'}; if (-not $existing) { Add-AzVirtualNetworkSubnetConfig -Name 'AzureFirewallSubnet' -VirtualNetwork $vnet -AddressPrefix '{firewallSubnetCidr}' | Set-AzVirtualNetwork } else { Write-Output 'AzureFirewallSubnet already exists' }
entries.get_command: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'AzureFirewallSubnet'} | Select-Object Name, AddressPrefix
evidence_commands: Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Select-Object Name, AddressPrefix
entries.notes: LAST RESORT: the AzureFirewallSubnet is created only together with the firewall (AZ-FW-002) and is not in Muster's default manifest (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.8). The name "AzureFirewallSubnet" is mandated by Azure and needs at least a /26.

entries.label: Create Network Security Group
entries.notes: Creates the primary Network Security Group (nsg-workload-cmmc) for the workload subnet. NSGs enforce layer-4 traffic filtering at the subnet level. Evidence proves the NSG resource exists and is ready for rule configuration (AZ-NSG-002 through AZ-NSG-004).

entries.label: Add NSG Rule — Deny All Inbound
entries.set_command: $nsg = Get-AzNetworkSecurityGroup -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nsg-workload-cmmc'; Add-AzNetworkSecurityRuleConfig -NetworkSecurityGroup $nsg -Name 'DenyAllInbound' -Description 'Deny all inbound traffic' -Protocol '*' -SourcePortRange '*' -DestinationPortRange '*' -SourceAddressPrefix '*' -DestinationAddressPrefix '*' -Access 'Deny' -Priority 4096 -Direction 'Inbound' | Set-AzNetworkSecurityGroup
entries.get_command: Get-AzNetworkSecurityGroup -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nsg-workload-cmmc' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SecurityRules | Where-Object Name -eq 'DenyAllInbound' | Select-Object -First 1 Name,Access,Direction,Priority,SourceAddressPrefix,DestinationPortRange | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
entries.notes: Adds a DenyAllInbound rule at the lowest priority (4096) to enforce deny-by-default inbound traffic per SC.L2-3.13.6. Only explicitly allowed rules at higher priority (lower number) can override this baseline deny. Evidence proves the deny-all-inbound posture is in place.

entries.label: Add NSG Rule — Deny All Outbound
entries.set_command: $nsg = Get-AzNetworkSecurityGroup -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nsg-workload-cmmc'; Add-AzNetworkSecurityRuleConfig -NetworkSecurityGroup $nsg -Name 'DenyAllOutbound' -Description 'Deny all outbound traffic' -Protocol '*' -SourcePortRange '*' -DestinationPortRange '*' -SourceAddressPrefix '*' -DestinationAddressPrefix '*' -Access 'Deny' -Priority 4096 -Direction 'Outbound' | Set-AzNetworkSecurityGroup
entries.get_command: Get-AzNetworkSecurityGroup -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nsg-workload-cmmc' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SecurityRules | Where-Object Name -eq 'DenyAllOutbound' | Select-Object -First 1 Name,Access,Direction,Priority,SourceAddressPrefix,DestinationPortRange | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
entries.notes: Adds a DenyAllOutbound rule at priority 4096: deny-by-default egress (SC.L1-3.13.1, SC.L2-3.13.6). Paired with the standard-boundary allow rules AZ-NSG-006 (443 to named service tags) and AZ-NSG-007 (443 to the Microsoft 365 GCC High ranges); without them a VM behind this NSG reaches no Microsoft service (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.1, §4.3 SB-2).

entries.label: Add NSG Rule — Allow Bastion Inbound
entries.set_command: $nsg = Get-AzNetworkSecurityGroup -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nsg-workload-cmmc'; Add-AzNetworkSecurityRuleConfig -NetworkSecurityGroup $nsg -Name 'AllowBastionInbound' -Description 'Allow inbound from AzureBastionSubnet' -Protocol 'Tcp' -SourcePortRange '*' -DestinationPortRange @('22','3389') -SourceAddressPrefix '{bastionSubnetCidr}' -DestinationAddressPrefix 'VirtualNetwork' -Access 'Allow' -Priority 100 -Direction 'Inbound' | Set-AzNetworkSecurityGroup
entries.notes: Allows TCP 22/3389 inbound from the Bastion subnet only. Only for a tenant that opts in to Bastion (AZ-BAS-001/002, recurring and two-person); the standard boundary has no inbound allow at all, and administration goes through Azure Run Command under PIM-gated RBAC (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.6, §4.8). Making this entry conditional on the Bastion opt-in is a translation change (DEPTH-2).

entries.label: Associate NSG with Workload Subnet
entries.notes: Associates the nsg-workload-cmmc NSG with the snet-workload subnet, activating the deny-by-default rules (AZ-NSG-002/003) and Bastion allow rule (AZ-NSG-004). Without this association, NSG rules are not enforced. Evidence proves the workload subnet has active boundary protection.

entries.label: Create Network Watcher
entries.set_command: $existing = Get-AzNetworkWatcher | Where-Object {$_.Location -eq '{location}'}; if (-not $existing) { New-AzNetworkWatcher -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nw-{location}' -Location '{location}' } else { Write-Output "Network Watcher already exists in $($existing.ResourceGroupName) - no action needed" }
entries.get_command: Get-AzNetworkWatcher | Where-Object {$_.Location -eq '{location}'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ResourceGroupName, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json
evidence_commands: Get-AzNetworkWatcher | Where-Object {$_.Location -eq '{location}'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ResourceGroupName, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Creates a Network Watcher in the tenant's region (QUESTIONS P-11: region from {location}, no hard-coded region) unless one already exists there. Azure creates one per region automatically in most subscriptions. Free (no meter); flow logs (AZ-NW-002) are retired.

entries.retired_reason: Microsoft stopped allowing new NSG flow logs in June 2025; VNet flow logs (AO F-14) replace them. Kept for reference; do not plan it.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: NSG flow logs to storage (retired by Microsoft, June 2025)

entries.label: Enable NSG Flow Logs to Log Analytics
entries.notes: Enables NSG flow logs in JSON v2 format, directing traffic metadata to the immutable log storage account. Flow logs provide the raw network traffic data needed for AU.L2-3.3.1 audit logging and AU.L2-3.3.2 user-traceable activity. Evidence proves flow logging is active on the workload NSG.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: 1 static IP, only with the firewall

entries.label: Create Firewall Public IP
entries.notes: LAST RESORT: the firewall public IP, created only together with AZ-FW-002 (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.8). Recurring and two-person. The standard boundary has no firewall and no public IP except the one gated egress IP of AZ-NET-007.

cost_gate.estimate_basis: 1 firewall x 730 h; data processed extra

entries.label: Create Azure Firewall
entries.set_command: $policy = Get-AzFirewallPolicy -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'cmmc-fw-policy' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (-not $policy) { $policy = New-AzFirewallPolicy -Name 'cmmc-fw-policy' -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Location '{location}' -ThreatIntelMode 'Deny' }; $pip = Get-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'pip-fw-cmmc'; $vnet = Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}'; New-AzFirewall -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'fw-cmmc' -Location '{location}' -VirtualNetwork $vnet -PublicIpAddress $pip -FirewallPolicyId $policy.Id -SkuTier 'Premium'
entries.notes: LAST RESORT (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.7; founder ruling 2026-10-31): recurring, two-person, off by default. The standard boundary (SB, spec §4.3: AZ-POL-001, AZ-NSG-002/003/006/007, AZ-SEP-001, AZ-VM-005) meets SC.L1-3.13.1 and SC.L2-3.13.6 without it. As written this entry filters nothing: no route table sends traffic to the firewall and no application or network rule collection exists (spec §4.1). An approved firewall must come with that route table and those rule collections (open follow-up, FIN-40 log). The SKU tier is Premium here; spec §4.8 wants a variable defaulting to Basic, and Basic also needs a management subnet and a second public IP (open item, DEPTH-2). DP-1 needs the no_other_means justification.

standard_alternative: none: no VMs in a cloud-native enclave; administer through Azure Run Command under PIM

entries.label: Create Bastion Public IP
entries.notes: Creates a Standard SKU static public IP for the Azure Bastion host. This IP is the only public-facing endpoint in the architecture and is locked down by Bastion service requirements. Evidence proves the public IP resource exists for Bastion deployment.

standard_alternative: none: no VMs in a cloud-native enclave; administer through Azure Run Command under PIM

entries.label: Create Azure Bastion Host
entries.notes: Deploys an Azure Bastion Standard host for secure, browser-based RDP/SSH access to VMs without exposing public IPs. Bastion satisfies SC.L1-3.13.1 by routing all administrative remote access through a managed access control point. Evidence proves Bastion is deployed on the correct VNet.

entries.label: Create Private Endpoint for Key Vault
entries.set_command: $existing = Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-kv*'}; if (-not $existing) { $kv = Get-AzKeyVault -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -VaultName '{keyVaultName}'; $conn = New-AzPrivateLinkServiceConnection -Name 'pe-conn-kv' -PrivateLinkServiceId $kv.ResourceId -GroupId 'vault'; New-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'pe-kv-prod' -Location '{location}' -Subnet (Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object Name -eq 'snet-workload') -PrivateLinkServiceConnection $conn } else { Write-Output "Key Vault private endpoint already exists: $($existing.Name)" }
entries.get_command: Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -WarningAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-kv*'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
evidence_commands: Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-kv*'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Creates a private endpoint for Key Vault on the workload subnet, removing public network exposure for cryptographic key operations. Private endpoints satisfy SC.L2-3.13.6 deny-by-default by restricting Key Vault access to the VNet only. Evidence proves the private endpoint is provisioned.

entries.label: Create Private Endpoint for Storage Account
entries.set_command: $existing = Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-storage*' -or $_.Name -like 'pe-sa*'}; if (-not $existing) { $sa = Get-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{storageAccountName}'; $conn = New-AzPrivateLinkServiceConnection -Name 'pe-conn-sa' -PrivateLinkServiceId $sa.Id -GroupId 'blob'; New-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'pe-storage-blob-prod' -Location '{location}' -Subnet (Get-AzVirtualNetwork -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name '{vnetName}' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Subnets | Where-Object Name -eq 'snet-workload') -PrivateLinkServiceConnection $conn } else { Write-Output "Storage private endpoint already exists: $($existing.Name)" }
entries.get_command: Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -WarningAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-storage*' -or $_.Name -like 'pe-sa*'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 3
evidence_commands: Get-AzPrivateEndpoint -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' | Where-Object {$_.Name -like 'pe-storage*' -or $_.Name -like 'pe-sa*'} | Select-Object Name, Location, ProvisioningState | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: Creates a private endpoint for the blob storage account on the workload subnet, ensuring audit log writes traverse the private network only. This satisfies SC.L2-3.13.6 by eliminating public blob access to the immutable log store. Evidence proves the storage private endpoint is provisioned.

entries.label: Create Automation Account
entries.notes: Creates an Azure Automation account for scheduled compliance runbooks (evidence collection, drift detection, key rotation). The automation account is the execution host for recurring CMMC compliance tasks. Evidence proves the account exists and is provisioned in the correct resource group.

entries.label: Assign System Managed Identity to Automation Account
entries.notes: Assigns a system-managed identity to the Automation account via REST API (Az PowerShell does not expose the identity property directly). Captures automationMiPrincipalId for RBAC grants in AZ-AUTO-003. Evidence proves identity-based authentication is configured for automation runbooks.

entries.label: Grant Automation MI RBAC Roles (Security Reader, LAR on LAW, SBDC on Storage, KV Crypto User on KV)
entries.set_command: New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{automationMiPrincipalId}' -RoleDefinitionName 'Security Reader' -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}'; New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{automationMiPrincipalId}' -RoleDefinitionName 'Log Analytics Reader' -Scope '{lawResourceId}'; New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{automationMiPrincipalId}' -RoleDefinitionName 'Storage Blob Data Contributor' -Scope '{storageResourceId}'; New-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{automationMiPrincipalId}' -RoleDefinitionName 'Key Vault Crypto User' -Scope '{kvResourceId}'
entries.get_command: $assignments = Get-AzRoleAssignment -ObjectId '{automationMiPrincipalId}'; @{ hasSubScope = ($assignments | Where-Object { $_.Scope -eq '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}' -and $_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Security Reader' }) -ne $null; hasLawScope = ($assignments | Where-Object { $_.Scope -like '*/workspaces/{lawWorkspaceName}' -and $_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Log Analytics Reader' }) -ne $null; hasStorageScope = ($assignments | Where-Object { $_.Scope -like '*/storageAccounts/{storageAccountName}' -and $_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Storage Blob Data Contributor' }) -ne $null; hasKvScope = ($assignments | Where-Object { $_.Scope -like '*/vaults/{keyVaultName}' -and $_.RoleDefinitionName -eq 'Key Vault Crypto User' }) -ne $null } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
entries.notes: Grants the Automation account managed identity four RBAC roles: Security Reader (subscription-wide), Log Analytics Reader (LAW), Storage Blob Data Contributor (storage), and Key Vault Crypto User (KV). These are the minimum permissions for compliance runbooks per AC.L1-3.1.1 least privilege.

entries.label: Onboard Sentinel to Log Analytics Workspace
entries.notes: Uses az CLI syntax (az rest) — required for operations without Az PowerShell cmdlet equivalents.

entries.label: Enable Sentinel Azure Activity Data Connector

The SET registers the subscription's EncryptionAtHost feature first when it is not registered. The generated local admin password is never stored: Key Vault is not in the standard baseline (founder ruling OQ-4), so the password is discarded and recovery uses the free VM Access password-reset extension under the customer's own Azure role (BA-10); CES holds nothing. Trusted Launch needs a Generation 2 image, so {vmImage} must name a Gen2 image. The VM is placed on snet-workload behind the NSG deny-all rules. A VM is a recurring cost: off by default, behind DP-1 and DP-2.

entries.label: VM Encryption at Host (platform-managed keys, free)

entries.notes: SP-12 (SECRETS-PLAN.md): zero-cost encryption at rest for the VM that holds ces.db and the evidence store. Encryption at host plus Azure server-side encryption with platform-managed keys covers the OS and data disks, the temp disk and the caches, at no cost (options paper O7). Azure Disk Encryption (Set-AzVMDiskEncryptionExtension, a Key Vault-backed BitLocker extension) is no longer used, so Disk Backup keeps working (packaging record line 178) and no Key Vault is needed. Turning encryption at host on for an existing VM needs it stopped, so the SET stops, updates and starts the VM only when the setting is off; AZ-VM-001 creates the VM with it on, so on a first run the GET finds it and nothing restarts. Planned only together with AZ-VM-001 (cost_gate.requires_entries). It no longer claims SC.L2-3.13.10 (no key is managed); SC.L2-3.13.16 is inherited from the platform.

entries.notes: Standard boundary layers SB-2 and SB-3 (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.3): one outbound allow on TCP 443 (priority 210) to the IPv4 ranges Microsoft publishes for the US Government GCC High instance (endpoint web service instance USGovGCCHigh, service areas Exchange and Common), so the CES VM reaches Exchange Online, Graph and the sign-in endpoints behind Deny-All-Outbound. Free (no meter). The SET re-reads the list each time it runs; the scheduled refresh on the CES VM is SB-3 (CG-10). The caller needs outbound HTTPS to endpoints.office.com when this runs. Which service area carries Graph in GCC High is unconfirmed. Not yet served by the simulator (DEPTH-9a). DEPTH-2 (2026-10-31): the ranges are no longer fetched inside the SET. They arrive as {m365Ipv4Ranges}, a comma-separated list of the IPv4 ranges the Microsoft 365 endpoint service (instance USGovGCCHigh, service areas Exchange and Common, TCP 443) publishes, supplied by the scheduled refresh (SB-3, CG-10). Until a manifest supplies it, the translator leaves this entry out (unresolved variable), so no configuration command makes a live web call.

entries.label: Explicit Egress Public IP for the CES VM (SB outbound floor)
entries.set_command: $pip = Get-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'pip-ces-egress-{vmName}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if (-not $pip) { $pip = New-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'pip-ces-egress-{vmName}' -Location '{location}' -Sku 'Standard' -AllocationMethod 'Static' }; $nic = Get-AzNetworkInterface -ResourceGroupName '{resourceGroup}' -Name 'nic-{vmName}'; $a = Get-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'CES-No-NIC-Public-IP' -Scope '/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroup}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($a -and -not (Get-AzPolicyExemption -Name 'ces-egress-{vmName}' -Scope $nic.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { $null = New-AzPolicyExemption -Name 'ces-egress-{vmName}' -PolicyAssignment $a -Scope $nic.Id -ExemptionCategory 'Waiver' -Description 'SB-1 exemption for the one explicit egress IP (AZ-NET-007)' }; $nic.IpConfigurations[0].PublicIpAddress = $pip; $nic | Set-AzNetworkInterface | Select-Object Name,@{N='PublicIpId';E={$_.IpConfigurations[0].PublicIpAddress.Id}} | ConvertTo-Json
entries.notes: The outbound floor (COST-GATE-SPEC.md §4.4): once Azure's default outbound access is retired, a VM in a private subnet reaches nothing without an explicit outbound method. This is the cheapest one: one Standard static public IP on the CES VM's network card, about $4.56 a month (US Gov list). Recurring, so off by default behind DP-1 and DP-2; not two-person. Inbound stays denied by the NSG (AZ-NSG-002) and the host firewall (AZ-VM-005). It adds the only SB-1 policy exemption (AZ-POL-001). It should be skipped when the tenant record names customer-owned egress; that condition is a translation change (DEPTH-2). The retirement date and Azure Government behaviour are unconfirmed. Not yet served by the simulator (DEPTH-9a).
